utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-01-45-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Gotovina, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please sit down, and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Mark McKeon. I'm joined at counsel table by Laurie Sartorio and our case manager, Donnica Henry Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. McKeon, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please. Microphone for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Luka Misetic from Chicago, Illinois, U.S.A., Defence counsel for General Gotovina. My fellow counsel, Mr. Greg Kehoe, I believe is being issued an order by the Registry today to be appointed was unable to attend this morning. He had to travel back to the United States and wished to express his regrets to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Misetic, and good morning to you. This is the first Status Conference in this case. The initial appearance of the accused, you will recall, took place on the 12th of December last year. I presided over that initial appearance myself. Now, pursuant to Rule 65 bis of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Status Conference needs to be convened periodically within a period of 120 days' interval in order to organise exchanges between the parties, and to ensure the expeditious preparation for trial, and to allow the accused to raise issues in relation to the case. Now, the agenda for today's Status Conference is necessarily shorter than one would expect it to be as we go along in the pre-trial phase, and I will deal first with some outstanding -- some pending motions. Now, there is first and foremost a Prosecution motion for non-disclosure of public -- to the public of supporting material filed on 11th January 2006. Now, at the time of the filing, you, Mr. Misetic, had not yet been confirmed as lead counsel to represent the accused. So duty counsel who had been appointed by the Registrar in the meantime, and to whom I wish to express the gratitude and appreciation of the Trial Chamber for his good work, he requested a stay of this motion until the issue of representation was finally resolved. This request was granted by my Trial Chamber on the 26th of January, and after the admittance of you as lead counsel, you requested the Chamber, on the 27th of March, that's barely two weeks ago, you filed a response to the motion. You asked the Trial Chamber, basically, on the 27th of March to file a response to the motion by the 4th of April. You will recall that I granted that motion, and I am appreciative that you have filed in time. In fact, I have received your response in relation to this motion, and I will discuss it with my colleagues, if necessary, and then I will hand down the decision very shortly. The second -- do you wish to add anything on this motion, Mr. McKeon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: The only thing I wish to add, Your Honour, is we're currently reviewing the response to see whether we think a reply to it would be necessary. And if we do wish to reply to this motion or the other pending motion, we'll seek leave to file the reply with our reply within the seven days provided under the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. McKeon, and please feel free to do that. The second pending motion relates to the Prosecution consolidated motion to amend the indictment and for joinder. Now, I need to explain the events here, and then I will be asking you, in particular, some questions to which I need a particular answer. On the 20th of February, as you recall, the Prosecution filed the motion I've just mentioned for joinder and -- and to amend the indictment seeking either for a joinder with -- of your case, Mr. Gotovina, with the case against the accused Cermak and Markac. This case, Cermak and Markac, is also one of the cases entrusted to Trial Chamber II, although I am not the Pre-Trial Judge in it. At the same time, the Prosecution, as I said, sought to amend the indictment in order to conform with the changes in the indictment for the accused Cermak and Markac as a result of preliminary motions filed in this latter case. Since the composition of the Pre-Trial Chamber for the case of Cermak and Markac was a different one as the Pre-Trial Chamber for this case, the President assigned the present Pre-Trial Chamber consisting of Judge Parker, Judge Van den Wyngaert and myself as the Bench that will decide upon the joinder motion. That is so that we make sure that there is a harmonisation between the two cases and one decision that will be uniform for both. On the 7th of March, both the accused Cermak and Markac filed their objections to the joinder motion. I don't know if you have become privy to that, if you have are aware of it, or if you have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were served with a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has filed these responses with its reply of the 13th of March. Also in relation to this motion, just a couple of days ago, counsel requested for an extension of time to respond until 4th April, as I said. This was granted and the Chamber has received the response, as I stated earlier, to this motion as well. Now, my problem is the following, Mr. Misetic. I have gone through your 4th April response to this motion, and it seems to me that although it primary attaches on the issue of the joinder, it does, however, deal with some of the elements of pleading in the indictment. Am I to consider your response of the 4th of April to be a full response also pursuant to Rule 72 of the Rules, that is, as a motion in itself challenging the facts in the form of the indictment, or do you still wish to file such a Rule 72 motion? I'm saying this because I consider it useful to take one overall decision relating both to the question of joinder and to the issue of any possible defects in the form of the joinder indictment at the same time. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. Our response to the motion was actually limited in the sense that it was a response to the Rule 50 aspect of their motion to amend the existing indictment into the proposed joinder indictment. We did not look at it from the perspective of Rule 72. It came to my attention I believe on Wednesday that I became concerned that the clock was ticking with respect to our Rule 72 motions, given the 30 days under the Rules that we would have to respond. So I contacted the Chambers to ask whether I should file a motion to extend that or not. So I guess the short answer is: We have not raised any Rule 72 objections at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It doesn't -- I do wish to clarify. I'm not certain at this point that we have any Rule 72 motions we wish to bring, but I would ask that we be given some time to further consider the issue and see whether we might have any issues either with respect to the form of the indictment or with respect to some jurisdictional issues that we might have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you so much, Mr. Misetic. That makes things clear, and I suspected this pretty much to be the case. So the position now is as follows. I'm giving you until Friday, the 21st of April, that is, basically a fortnight from today, time within which to file a motion pursuant to Rule 72, if you so wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just a point for clarification. It's a Rule 72 motion directed at the proposed joinder indictment and not the existing indictment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and we appreciate the extension of time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: After that, Prosecution will have until week after Friday, 28th of April, to file one consolidated reply to the filing of the Defence, which we already have, that is the one filed on the 4th of April, and the possible filing that we might have by the 21st; in other words, on the 28th, latest, you will address these two responses, one of which we have, one we are expecting by means of a consolidated response. Is that clear, Mr. McKeon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. If -- I just wanted a clarification. If we decide not to file a motion under Rule 72 and instead serve the Court with a notice that there won't be a motion, would that -- would it be seven days for reply from the date of such a notice or are we keeping the existing time frame so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If tomorrow you file a note indicating that you will not be filing the -- any motion on -- pursuant to Rule 72, then obviously I'm going to revise. There's no need to have the 28th of April limit then, because the Prosecution has been served with the 4th April motion in any case already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McKeon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only thing that I'm a bit concerned about, we -- first of all, we don't know if there will be a Rule 72 motion; but secondly, if there is we don't know how extensive it's going to be. Normally under the Rules we would be given 14 days to respond to such a motion, and I'm a bit concerned in the absence of knowing what it is that we are responding to that the time has been cut basically in half to seven days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, Mr. McKeon. But please do understand as well that as regards the response which you have already received on the 4th of April, I take it that you have started working on that and that -- in any case, you should be ready with your response on that within either seven or 14 days for that matter. If we won't have any response from -- any motion from the Defence pursuant to Rule 72, there is no reason why you shouldn't be prepared to file your response for the 4th April within 14 days from the 4th of April. So let's make that clear. If instead of that we do have a Rule 72 motion and it is more complicated than either you or I may have expected and there is need for a further seven days, I will of course consider such a request if and when it is made. But I wouldn't like to pre-empt any issues in the matter. I mean, the way I see it if there is a Rule 72 motion, I think seven days from that day to answer it should be -- should be enough. If they are not enough, we will consider any further request that you may have. If there is no Rule 72 motion, there is no reason why on the 18th of April you shouldn't be able to produce the -- your response for the 4th April motion -- Defence motion. All right. So -- or a response, rather. Did I make myself clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: You did, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- one -- I would expect you to be reasonable and please take it for granted that I and my Chamber will also be reasonable. So that disposes of the motions that I have expending. Now disclosure. Under Rule 66(A)(i), pursuant to this subrule, the Prosecutor should make available to the Defence in a language which the accused understands and within 30 days of the initial appearance of the accused copies of the supporting materials which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought as well as all prior to statements obtained by the Prosecution from the accused. The Chamber understands that - and I need a confirmation from you on this - the Chamber understands that such supporting material has been disclosed and that counsel for the accused has received all files upon assignment to this case. So let's start with you, Mr. McKeon. Do you confirm that you have fulfilled this phase of -- or this category of disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On January 11th, 2006, we disclosed the original supporting materials in this case. The only thing that I want to add to that is there is the pending motion on the redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: And -- so that we didn't essentially make that motion moot. We have redacted, as we've requested in the motion, the supporting materials, but of course if that motion is denied then we would re-disclose them out the redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And, Mr. Misetic, do you confirm that you have received the documents the Prosecution was under an obligation to disclose under this subrule?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have received on the 22nd of March from Mr. Knoops the supporting materials that he received from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Now, the other category of documents to be disclosed falls -- or is regulated by Rule 66(A)(ii) pursuant to which the Prosecutor shall make available to the Defence in a language which the accused understands copies of the statements of all witnesses the Prosecution intends to call to testify at trial, as well as all copies of all written statements taken in accordance with Rule 92 bis of the Rules within the time limit prescribed by the Trial Chamber or the Pre-Trial Judge. Now, I suppose you will both agree with me that we are still in the very early stages of the pre-trial stage and no dead-lines have been set for the time being. In accordance with Rule 65 ter (D)(ii), together with my Senior Legal Officer, a work-plan will be established for the further pre-trial preparations of this case. In the meantime, I enjoin you, Mr. McKeon, to do -- to keep this as a on-working -- this category of disclosure an on-working -- ongoing obligation on your part starting -- making yourself ready, putting yourself ready, for when it is necessary for us to establish a dead-line. In other words, I would expect you to have already started working on this. Much depends also on whether there will be a joinder or not, because obviously if there is no joinder the situation may change a little bit. So prior to the next Status Conference my Senior Legal Officer will be instructed by me to convene another 65 ter Conference, at which the work plan that we would have conceived will be elaborated in consultation with both of you. Mr. McKeon, may I ask you, at this stage - although I myself are not setting any dead-lines and I acknowledge that we are still in the early stages of the case - may I ask you at what stage you yourself or your office has arrived in preparing for Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We essentially have been sitting on the disclosure awaiting the appointment of counsel. We have basically everything that's already been disclosed in the Cermak case, which we're ready to put on the EDS system in this case. I think at this point the person in our office, the staff member, who is responsible for maintaining the custody of these records and the record-keeping is away until after Easter, but I expect that right after Easter we will be putting a large material on the EDS that include some of the written witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much for your cooperation, Mr. McKeon. Are there comments from your side on this category of disclosures, Mr. Misetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I take the word of my colleagues on the other side that it will be available after the 18th. I just wasn't sure whether that disclosure was in any way contingent upon the Trial Chamber's ruling on the motion for non-disclosure that the OTP had filed. In other words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To an extent, but to a minor extent I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, finally Rule 68(i) and (ii) disclosures. Have you already started disclosing or finished disclosing Rule 68 material, both paragraphs of Rule 68, the exculpatory one and the other one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be included in the materials that we disclose within the next couple of weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I thank you. According to me, there shouldn't be any further business to transact this morning, unless I see an indication from you that you would like to raise additional matters? I see none. All right. So, Mr. Gotovina, the Rules -- the Rules require me to ask you whether you would like to raise any matter relating to your health, physical or mental, as well as to the state of your detention, in other words, how you're being treated at the Detention Unit of -- of the Tribunal. If there is anything you would like to raise, please do it now. This is one of the reasons why we hold periodical Status Conferences, so that you are given the opportunity to come face-to-face with the Pre-Trial Judge and speak with all liberty, knowing that you will receive all the attention and all the protection that you need from me. Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no problems. Thank you for asking. Everything is in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Gotovina. So that brings to an end the -- today's Status Conference. Should there be any problems or matters that need to be addressed to between this Status Conference and the next, you will be of course approached by my Senior Legal Officer. We will be dealing with the outstanding motions with the utmost celerity. Of course the -- everything has to be decided in conjunction with the Cermak and Markac case so that we will -- probably be a decision for both contemporaneously and then we will take it up from there. All right. Thank you.
